meta_jurisdiction_context.sovereign_country_en: People's Republic of China (mainland sovereignty exercised over Hong Kong SAR)
meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (Hong Kong SAR), with separate company registry and AML/CFT regime under the Hong Kong Basic Law
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (common law retained under Article 8 of the Hong Kong Basic Law, applying the Companies Ordinance Cap. 622 and Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance Cap. 615, with a PRC civil-law overlay for cross-border UBO and beneficial-owner information obligations imposed on mainland entities)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Mainland and Hong Kong Closer Economic Partnership Arrangement (CEPA) - Investment Agreement
Mainland and Hong Kong Double Tax Arrangement for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income
CEPA Agreement on Trade in Services
Convention Abolishing the Requirement of Legalisation for Foreign Public Documents (Hague Apostille Convention), applied to China and Hong Kong SAR

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (revised 2021, effective 1 January 2022); Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information of Market Entities (PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3 [2024], effective 1 November 2024); Hong Kong Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Financing of Terrorism Ordinance (Cap. 615, Laws of Hong Kong); Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622, Laws of Hong Kong) and subsidiary regulations on company name, registered office and corporate records

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the mainland Chinese JV partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) / provincial-level Market Regulation Bureau of the People's Republic of China
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Sequence: (1) issue the original SAMR certificate; (2) notarize the Chinese-language duplicate at a PRC notary public; (3) obtain the Hague Apostille from the Consular Department of the PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs or its delegated provincial Foreign Affairs Office; (4) submit the apostilled file directly to the Hong Kong Companies Registry or banking institution. The apostille route and consular legalization are parallel and mutually exclusive; do NOT chain a consular legalization step.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the Hong Kong sponsor / co-investor company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong Companies Registry (under the Companies Ordinance Cap. 622)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Sequence: (1) obtain the certificate from the Companies Registry; (2) where the recipient requires foreign-use authentication, obtain the Hague Apostille from the High Court Authentication Office (Registry of the High Court of Hong Kong SAR) under the Authentication of Documents Ordinance (Cap. 34); (3) no consular legalization is added. Because Hong Kong is in the Apostille Convention, the apostille is conclusive and exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney (PoA) authorizing incorporation of the Sino-foreign JV and appointing local Hong Kong directors and company secretary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the mainland Chinese joint venture partner (corporate secretary certified)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Sequence: (1) certify the board minutes and PoA by the company secretary; (2) notarize the signature pages with a PRC notary public; (3) obtain a single Hague Apostille from the PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs or delegated provincial office; (4) deliver directly to Hong Kong counsel. Do not add any consular legalization because China is an Apostille Convention state.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (AoA) and Joint Venture Contract (JVC) of the proposed Hong Kong JV entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: All proposed JV parties (executed by authorized shareholders) and PRC notarial supervision
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Sequence: (1) execute the AoA and JVC in both Chinese and English; (2) notarize the execution blocks before a PRC notary public; (3) affix the Hague Apostille by the PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs or delegated provincial office; (4) file the English-language version with the Hong Kong Companies Registry. Consular legalization is inapplicable and must be omitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter issued by a Hong Kong authorized institution for the sponsor/co-investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong licensed bank (authorized institution under the Banking Ordinance Cap. 155)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Sequence: (1) the bank's branch manager/compliance officer signs and authenticates the letter; (2) if the recipient jurisdiction requires legalization, the High Court Authentication Office of Hong Kong SAR affixes the Hague Apostille; (3) apostille alone is used. If the issuing bank is instead situated in a non-Apostille state, use exclusively consular legalization at the PRC embassy or consulate of that state, and do not attempt to add an apostille chain.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All proposed directors, shareholders, beneficial owners, signatories, authorized representatives, counterparties and payment-rail beneficiaries must be screened against (i) mainland PRC PEP lists and the PBOC anti-money laundering monitoring list, (ii) Hong Kong Joint Financial Intelligence Unit (JFIU) guidance, (iii) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Non-SDN Consolidated Sanctions lists, (iv) United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, (v) UK, EU and domestic Hong Kong sanctions lists, and (vi) adverse media and PEP databases with a 25% UBO threshold and look-back extending to immediate family and close associates. Enhanced due diligence is required for any PEP, sanctions link, shell-company indication, or unexplained source of funds from trust or offshore arrangements, with escalation to the Money Laundering Reporting Officer and transaction freeze where any UN or OFAC match is confirmed.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Hong Kong Companies Registry - Integrated Companies Registry Information System (ICRIS) e-Registry online portal and name-search facility (www.icris.cr.gov.hk)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622), an English company name must consist of Roman letters and numerals; a Chinese name must use Traditional Chinese characters and must be a transliteration or recognized translation of the English name. The Registry tests phonetic, visual and semantic similarity against the existing register. For a bilingual JV, the four-tier naming doctrine requires the following to be fixed before filing: (1) full formal English name; (2) full formal Chinese name; (3) combined bilingual name; and (4) the abbreviated name used on contracts and invoicing, so that Stripe Billing descriptors and ACH Direct beneficiary names match the registered name on a pass-through basis.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, the applicant must use the ICRIS rejection code to correct and re-file before the original 30-day window expires; an extension is not automatic and requires a fresh reservation application supported by a written explanation. For formal appeal, Hong Kong counsel shall lodge with the Companies Registry a written appeal attaching legal submissions, evidence of distinctiveness, consent letters from any statutory regulator responsible for the sensitive token (e.g., HKMA for Bank), and a searchable comparison table of the refused name versus the existing register. If the appeal is refused, the applicant may contest the decision before the Administrative Appeals Board within 28 days, and should reserve judicial review rights; while the appeal is pending, the entity must not incorporate under the contested name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: The Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) requires a physical street address in Hong Kong for registered office service of process; a P.O. box is void. A virtual office is accepted only if it is a serviced office with a licensed company secretary and registered office agent, not a mere mail-drop. For a PropTech SaaS business with payment rails (Stripe Billing and ACH Direct), the Inland Revenue Department will assess whether the place of management and control is genuinely in Hong Kong, and banks conducting KYC under Cap. 615 will reject a shell-like virtual-mailbox profile because it lacks substance, auditable domestic management, and presence. Thus a virtual office is not permissible as the sole location; the JV must lease physical office space, hold management meetings there, keep board minutes there, and maintain local bank accounts, payroll and AML/CFT records there.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced inspection: (i) physical lease or ownership of a Hong Kong office; (ii) HK Employment Ordinance payroll and MPF enrollment records; (iii) original board minutes prepared and signed at the registered office; (iv)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622, Laws of Hong Kong), principally sections 67 and 68 on incorporation by registration, section 112 on company secretary requirements, section 474 on registered office, and the Companies (Fees) Regulations; Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310) for the mandatory Business Registration Certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies Registry, Hong Kong SAR, 28/F, Queensway Government Offices, 66 Queensway, Hong Kong; electronic filing through the e-Registry / eTC Online Portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Form NNC1, Statement of Capital, Memorandum of Association, Articles of Association, and the associated Business Registration Certificate application transmitted to the Inland Revenue Department.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Hong Kong does not impose a minimum paid-up capital requirement for a private company limited by shares. The subscribers may allot shares with a nominal value of HK$1.00 each or such other amount as stated in the Statement of Capital. There is no escrow or blocked-account capital rule under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622). The opening bank may, in its commercial discretion, require initial working capital deposits or make regulatory KYC inquiries, but no statutory capital deposit or escrow is mandated.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS of [●] Limited (the Company), passed by unanimous written resolution on [date] at the registered office of the Company pursuant to the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) and the Articles of Association of the Company. WHEREAS the Company was duly incorporated in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region on [incorporation date] with registration number [●]; and WHEREAS the subscribers have agreed to subscribe for ordinary shares in the capital of the Company as set out in the Application for Incorporation; and WHEREAS the directors of the Company are required to adopt a formal resolution for the proper governance of the Company, including the adoption of the registered office, the appointment of statutory officers, the issue of shares, and the opening of banking facilities. NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS HEREBY RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS: 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT: RESOLVED THAT the subscribers initial share capital, consisting of [●] ordinary shares of HK$1.00 each, be and is hereby allotted and issued to the subscribers in proportion to their respective subscriptions, credited as fully or partially paid to the extent set forth in the directors statement of capital. The directors be and are hereby authorized to issue share certificates under the common seal or under electronic signature arrangement and to enter the allotment in the register of members. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE: RESOLVED THAT the registered office of the Company be and is hereby established at [●], Hong Kong, and that the directors be authorized to file the requisite notice of situation of the registered office with the Companies Registry and to receive all statutory correspondence and service of process at such address. 3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: RESOLVED THAT the opening of banking facilities with [●] Bank be and is hereby approved. The directors, jointly with any two of [director names], be and are hereby authorized to execute account opening forms, sign mandates, issue instructions, and operate bank accounts within their discretion and in accordance with the Companies Ordinance and all anti-money laundering policies of the bank. 4. STATUTORY OFFICERS: RESOLVED THAT [●] be and is hereby appointed as Company Secretary, that [●] and [●] be appointed as Directors, and that [●] be appointed as Auditor of the Company, each to hold office in accordance with the Articles and Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622), with such appointments taking effect immediately. 5. CORPORATE GOVERNANCE AND FILINGS: RESOLVED THAT the directors be authorized to prepare and file all statutory returns, to adopt board policies on conflicts of interest and internal controls, and to exercise all powers of the Company as provided by law. This resolution was duly signed by all directors and shall be filed in the statutory books of the Company. Upon deletion of bracketed placeholders, the resolution constitutes a binding and enforceable corporate act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Clearance and Constitutional Document Drafting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry Hong Kong SAR - Electronic Services Delivery (eTC) Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search on the Companies Registry online integrated search facility. Select an English name ending with Limited and ensure no identical or confusingly similar name is registered. Prepare the Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association, including provisions governing share capital, director powers, and indemnity. For a Sino-foreign joint venture, confirm the China parent company corporate authorization and board consent is notarized and legalized for use in Hong Kong if required. Submit the chosen name and constitution drafts to the corporate service provider for final review before e-filing.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and constitutional documents of the China parent company
Board resolution of the China parent authorizing formation of the Hong Kong JV entity
Notarized copy of the parent company current registered address and directors list
Proposed memorandum and articles of association for the Hong Kong company
Shareholder identity documents and register of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the company name as undesirable or confusingly similar, promptly submit a revised name through the eTC portal and pay the applicable amendment fee. If documents are rejected for incompleteness, cure by uploading certified translations or corrected shareholder details within seven days of the requisition.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Application Submission and Statutory Fees Payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry Hong Kong SAR - e-Registry / eTC Portal for Form NNC1
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Incorporation Form NNC1 and the statement of capital. Attach the executed Articles of Association and submit electronically through the eTC portal. Include the intended registered office address, company secretary, director particulars, and subscriber details. Ensure the company secretary is either an individual ordinarily resident in Hong Kong or a recognized corporate body with its registered office or place of business in Hong Kong. Pay the Companies Registry incorporation fee and the Business Registration levy concurrently. Retain the electronic acknowledgement bearing the date and time of submission.
required_dossiers: Form NNC1 duly signed by all subscribers
Memorandum and Articles of Association
Statement of capital and initial shareholdings
Identity proof for directors and subscribers
Consent to act forms NNC3 if required
Parent corporate authorization and agent appointment form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is suspended by the Companies Registry, comply with the requisition letter by submitting missing consents or clarifications within seven days. If constitution provisions are unlawful or inconsistent with the Companies Ordinance, amend the Articles and resubmit. The Registrar may issue a non-compliance notice requiring corrected filing before certificate issuance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration Certificate and Inland Revenue Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department - Business Registration Office via eTC or IRD counter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, the Companies Registry transmits the completed NNC1 data to the Business Registration Office. The Business Registration Certificate will be issued upon settlement of prescribed fee. For a private company, this certificate evidences tax enrollment and should be obtained within one month of incorporation. Verify the registered address, legal entity identity, and business description align with the planned PropTech SaaS services. If using Stripe Billing or ACH Direct, obtain a certified copy of the Business Registration Certificate for banking KYC and payment processor onboarding.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Business Registration application and fee acknowledgement
Proof of address of the registered office
Directors and shareholders identity particulars
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Business Registration Certificate is not issued electronically due to fee non-payment, pay the outstanding levy immediately through the eTC portal. For an incorrect company name or address, apply to the Inland Revenue Department within fourteen days for amendment and provide supporting evidence of the corrected registered office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Statutory Filings and Corporate Book Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry via eTC for Form NR1 and ND2A; corporate services provider for statutory registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File any post-incorporation notices to the Companies Registry, including notice of situation of registered office using Form NR1 and particulars of directors and company secretary using Form ND2A, within fifteen days of any change. Set up the registered office, statutory registers of members, directors, charges, and seals. Draft, execute, and retain the first board resolution. Issue share certificates to subscribers and approve the opening of bank accounts. For a joint venture, prepare a shareholders agreement annex documenting board composition, deadlock and veto rights, ensuring consistency with the Articles of Association.
required_dossiers: Form NR1 if registered address differs from NNC1
Form ND2A or ND2B with director and secretary particulars
First board resolution text
Statement of capital
Registered office address verification document
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a late filing penalty is imposed, file the relevant notification with a letter of mitigating circumstances and pay the late fee. For incorrect particulars, submit an amended form within seven days and attach a declaration from directors confirming the corrected information.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Sector-Specific Licensing Confirmation and Banking AML Onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Hong Kong Monetary Authority licensed bank; verification against Hong Kong business and licensing registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm that ISIC 6201 computer programming and SaaS PropTech activities do not require a manufacturing, chemical, assembly, warehousing, or environmental license. If the company will hire employees, register with the Mandatory Provident Fund Schemes Authority. Open a corporate bank account with a licensed bank, presenting the incorporation certificate, business registration certificate, first board resolution, directors passport copies, organizational chart, and a business description. Complete AML due diligence forms, sign account signatory mandates, and connect payment rails such as Stripe Billing and ACH Direct. Retain a written opinion confirming that no industrial or physical licensing clearance is required for pure digital services.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Business Registration Certificate
First board resolution with banking authorization
Directors identity and address proofs
Parent company corporate registry search
Payment processor agreements
MPF employer registration confirmation if hiring
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If bank account onboarding is queried, supplement with certified English translations, audited parent company financial statements, and a business plan demonstrating source of funds and beneficial ownership transparency. If any licensing status is challenged, obtain a formal exemption or confirmation letter from the relevant government agency or engage counsel to clarify scope.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - no manufacturing, chemical, assembly, warehousing, or physical real-estate operation in scope; ISIC 6201 is computer programming and SaaS PropTech digital service activity.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - pure digital PropTech SaaS; no operating license required under Hong Kong industrial licensing regimes.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - Environmental Protection Department (EPD) Hong Kong, if and only if a physical project is later established.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable / Exempt by absence of designated industrial project under the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (Cap. 413); no physical facility, no EIA report, no environmental registration.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no point-source wastewater discharge, no VOC emissions, and no hazardous waste generation. For any general office IT scrap disposal, the company must follow the Waste Disposal Ordinance (Cap. 354) and applicable producer responsibility schemes; no industrial effluent or air emission thresholds apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable to the core digital software activity. If a general Hong Kong office is leased, the premises must be covered by a landlord fire certificate and fire safety compliance under the Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123), and the employer must comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Ordinance (Cap. 509). No Civil Defense fire permit is required for pure office, programming, or SaaS operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA), operating the electronic tax administration portal known as the 'E-Tax Bureau' (电子税务局; however the official English interface is referred to as the 'E-Tax Bureau' or 'Online Tax Payment Service' at etax.chinatax.gov.cn). For Hong Kong SAR: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), with electronic services via the 'GovHK' portal and the IRD's 'eTAX' electronic filing platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture established in mainland China, the enterprise is required to complete industrial and commercial registration with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR). Following issuance of the business license, the taxpayer must, within 30 days, complete tax registration at the competent county-level or district-level STA office where the registered address is located. The STA assigns an 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which serves as the enterprise's Tax Identification Number (TIN) for all tax filings, including VAT and corporate income tax. The foreign joint venture partners must provide certified copies of their home-country registration certificates, passport copies of legal representatives, and the joint venture contract and articles of association. For the Hong Kong SAR entity involved in this cross-border structure, the corporate vehicle is registered with the Companies Registry and then obtains a Business Registration Certificate (BRC) from the Inland Revenue Department. The IRD assigns a Commercial Registration Number (CR number) that functions as the Hong Kong taxpayer identification number. Where the Hong Kong entity carries on a business in Hong Kong and supplies taxable goods or services, it must register for Goods and Services Tax only if Hong Kong had implemented GST; currently Hong Kong does not impose VAT/GST, though customs duties and profits tax apply. If the Chinese JV engages in export activities, it must additionally complete foreign trade operator registration and customs registration with the General Administration of Customs of the People's Republic of China (GACC), obtaining a Customs Registration Code (10-digit customs code) linked to its USCC, and must also register for the export tax rebate system with the competent tax authority.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture is a Chinese resident enterprise subject to entity-level Corporate Income Tax under the Enterprise Income Tax Law of the People's Republic of China and is not eligible for pass-through or check-the-box treatment. Hong Kong SAR generally follows a territorial source principle for Profits Tax, and no hybrid mismatch election is available for the mainland China entity. Mainland China does not provide a check-the-box classification regime comparable to the United States.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Under the Measures for the Administration of Value-Added Tax Identification of Small-Scale Taxpayers, the annual VAT-registered sales threshold is RMB 5,000,000 (five million Renminbi). However, any enterprise established as a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture is generally required to obtain general VAT taxpayer status if its annual turnover exceeds RMB 5 million or if it has a fixed place of business and applies the general method of VAT calculation. Small-scale taxpayers with annual sales not exceeding RMB 5 million may alternatively register under the simplified levy method with a 3% collection rate, but the standard general VAT rate applicable to software-as-a-service and technology services supplied to business customers is 6%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mainland China operates the nationwide 'New e-Invoice' (数电票 / fully digitalized electronic invoice) system, rolled out by the STA. Fully digitalized electronic invoices use a unified electronic invoice format without physical paper, carry an anti-forgery electronic stamp encrypted with an official tax-control code, and are issued through the E-Tax Bureau platform or approved tax-UKey / ERP integration channels. The system requires real-time reporting of issued and received invoices to the STA's electronic invoice service platform through API-based or web-based clearance. Businesses must use official tax control devices or the new digital e-invoice service to generate invoices, and invoice data is automatically transmitted for comparison against VAT returns. For cross-border e-commerce exports, the customs clearance process is administered through the GACC 'single window' integrated platform, and ordinary VAT invoices must be reported by purchasers in the VAT invoice verification platform when claiming input VAT credits. Non-resident digital service suppliers without a physical presence in China are not generally required to issue Chinese VAT invoices for exports; however export transactions must be supported by formal contracts, customs declarations where goods are involved, and foreign exchange receipts.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exported goods sold by a Chinese registered enterprise to overseas customers are zero-rated for VAT, provided the goods are physically exported and customs export procedures are completed. For software-as-a-service and cloud-based PropTech services, China's VAT regime zero-rates the export of software products and certain digital services where the recipient is outside mainland China and the service is supplied wholly outside China, or qualifies as exported services under Caishui [2016] No. 36. Eligible offshore services include software as a service, data processing, and information technology services provided to overseas entities and paid for in foreign currency. The zero-rating applies only where the service is rendered to a non-resident enterprise, the service is not consumed within mainland China, and the enterprise retains contemporaneous documentation proving the export nature. Under Caishui [2016] No. 36 and the STA's definitions, cross-border sales of services may be exempted or zero-rated after filing the Cross-Border Tax Declaration Schedule and submitting relevant documentary evidence to the competent tax authority for review. For the Hong Kong SAR side, Hong Kong does not levy VAT, so no export zero-rating claim arises; profits tax on export-related income follows the territorial source principle.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Customs Clearance Form / Export Goods Customs Declaration Form) generated by the China International Trade Single Window, showing the export customs registration number
Bill of Lading (B/L) issued by the shipping carrier evidencing physical export from a Chinese port
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) issued by a designated foreign exchange bank evidencing payment in convertible foreign currency from the overseas buyer
Export VAT invoice (ordinary VAT invoice or special VAT export invoice) as legally required for export sales
Foreign exchange verification form (Export Collection and Settlement Verification) under the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) electronic system
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Under the Measures for Administration of Value-Added Tax on Exported Goods and Services, failure to repatriate foreign exchange within 180 days from the date of export declaration may result in the export sale being treated as domestic sales, requiring the taxpayer to pay VAT at the applicable rate (6% for technology services) and Corporate Income Tax adjustments, plus late payment surcharges. If the exporter submits false customs declarations, uses counterfeit documentation such as forged bills of lading, or engages in fraudulent export tax rebate schemes, the tax authority will disallow the zero-rating, claw back any exemptions or refunds, impose a penalty of 50% to 500% of the tax evaded under the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Suppression of Tax Evasion and Tax Refusal, and refer the case to customs anti-smuggling authorities or police for criminal prosecution. Additional sanctions include revocation of tax registration or export tax rebate qualification, a tax trust blacklist designation, blocking of export rebate applications, and customs credit downgrade under the AEO mutual recognition framework.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Hong Kong operates a completely open capital account system with no foreign exchange controls. The Hong Kong dollar is freely convertible into all major currencies, and the linked exchange rate system ensures stability against the US dollar (7.75-7.85 HKD/USD). Current account transactions, including profit remittances and dividends from a Hong Kong entity, are unrestricted and require merely proper board authorization. Capital account transactions such as equity injections and loan repayments also enjoy full liberalization. However, for a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture with a People's Republic of China (PRC) shareholder, the Chinese side must navigate the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) capital account controls governing outbound direct investment and repatriation of dividends back to the mainland. Specifically, the PRC shareholder must obtain prior approval/filing from NDRC and MOFCOM for its foreign investment, and remittances must be channeled through a designated Chinese bank with a valid foreign exchange business registration. The use of offshore RMB (CNH) in Hong Kong is unrestricted, but conversion between CNH and onshore CNY is only permitted through licensed banks within the mainland's trade settlement framework. Overall, the Hong Kong entity enjoys pristine convertibility, while cross-border flows involving mainland China require dual regulatory compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender requirements are imposed by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority. Exporters may hold, convert, or remit foreign currency proceeds freely without any conversion ratio or timeline. For mainland Chinese parents with direct export operations, SAFE requires repatriation within 180 days of export declaration, but no mandatory conversion ratio applies; the broader group should observe the Chinese external debt and receipt verification rules.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited (HSBC)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility rating with strict legal boundaries. Hong Kong-incorporated entities may onboard to licensed digital EMI platforms (e.g., Airwallex, Statrys, Neat) that operate under HKMA's Stored Value Facility or Money Service Operator licensing regime. These EMIs are legally permitted to service the JV for multi-currency transactional banking, SaaS collections through Stripe/ACH, and cross-border AP/AR settlement. However, they are not authorized to offer deposit-taking, trade finance (LC), or capital account custody. As such, EMIs should be positioned as supplementary payment rail, with the primary treasury relationship held at Tier-1 commercial banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: At least one statutory director (preferably the controlling shareholder) and the company secretary must attend an in-person KYC interview at the chosen bank's branch in Hong Kong. A remote biometric video interview is possible for low-risk fully digital companies at selected banks (e.g., HSBC Business Direct), subject to final compliance approval. Consular proxy opening is not recognized; a non-resident director must visit Hong Kong or authorize a local corporate services provider with a limited Power of Attorney, though successful acceptance is at the bank's discretion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancies in beneficial ownership where the PRC parent has multi-layered shareholding, causing unclear ultimate controlling persons and inconsistent identification evidence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete group ownership chart from each ultimate natural person to the Hong Kong entity; notarized passports of all individuals holding 10% or more interest; certified business licenses of every intermediate holding company; certificate of incumbency; JV agreement; and a board resolution explicitly outlining the commercial purpose of the Hong Kong JV.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unsubstantiated source of start-up capital from mainland China that may be perceived as circumventing PRC outbound direct investment (ODI) regulations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Stamped ODI approval certificate from NDRC and MOFCOM; SAFE Foreign Exchange Registration Form; original SWIFT remittance advice showing purpose code 621011; three years of audited PRC parent financial statements; corporate bank statements showing accumulation of funds; and a signed shareholder loan agreement (if applicable).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border SaaS revenue collection triggers potential exposure to sanctioned jurisdictions or prohibited merchants through anonymous digital signups.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Platform geo-blocking proof (IP and address level), customer onboarding policy with restricted country list, ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type II certificates, evidence of Stripe/ACH third-party KYC validation, and a notarized declaration confirming no OFAC, UN, or EU-listed entities are served.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Related-party outbound payments to the PRC parent for royalties or services could be mischaracterized as tax evasion or unlawful external debt.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transfer pricing documentation under HK DIPN 58/59; counterparty contracts with benchmarking analysis; board minutes proving arm's length commercial agreements; historical bank statements of identical recurring payments; and the PRC parent's VAT/profit tax filing index for the relevant period.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: PRC parent must complete ODI filing with MOFCOM and NDRC, then obtain the SAFE foreign exchange registration and remit via SWIFT MT103 using purpose code 'Overseas Direct Investment' (business nature code 621011). The Hong Kong entity designates a capital escrow account at a Tier-1 bank and presents the JV agreement, board resolution, and capital verification certificate issued by a Hong Kong certified public accountant after receipt. Currency must be USD or HKD for ease of verification, though ultimately conversion is unrestricted.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for immediate settlement of cloud service fees, licensing, and marketing costs with purpose code 22S (Software & IP) or 39 (Service Fees). For procurement of server hardware or high-value infrastructure, issue an irrevocable at-sight Commercial Letter of Credit confirmed by a top-tier bank. For recurring small-value disbursements to vendors, Documentary Collections offer a lower cost alternative but involve longer settlement cycles. The primary clearing rail remains SWIFT, with ACH only for US-dollar-denominated receivables from SaaS customers routed via Stripe settlements to the operating account.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards for HKD/USD and CNH/USD trades with an authorized institution in Hong Kong, maximum tenor 12 months, collateralized under ISDA CSA.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on onshore CNY to hedge cross-border royalty or procurement payments, executed with a bank holding a valid CNH trading license.
Cross-currency swaps to swap HKD debt service into USD or CNH, subject to HKMA 'non-centrally cleared margin rules' for qualified collateral.
FX options (plain vanilla call/put) on CNH or USD to hedge quarterly subscription revenue and dividend remittance timing risk without unlimited downside.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Form NAR1) for private company limited by shares
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after the return date, normally the anniversary of incorporation; for example, if incorporated on 7 April, the Annual Return must be delivered by 18 May each year. Companies that have not validly changed their accounting reference period remain anchored to the incorporation anniversary for return-date purposes.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If delivered after the 42-day period, the Companies Registry applies the higher fee scale under the Companies (Fees and Forms) Regulation, escalating from HK$420 to HK$3,355 depending on the length of delay and nominal share capital band. Non-delivery is an offence; the company and every responsible officer may be fined up to HK$50,000, with a daily default fine of up to HK$1,000 for continuing non-compliance. Where the Annual Return is persistently omitted, the Registrar may commence administrative strike-off by publishing a notice in the Government Gazette and, after the statutory objection period of at least 3 months, dissolve the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business Registration Certificate renewal and payment of the annual business registration fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the expiry date printed on the current Business Registration Certificate; for most companies this is an annual renewal, although the Business Registration Office may issue a 3-year certificate where elected. The exact renewal window is from the certificate anniversary date unless the Business Registration Office prescribes a different cycle.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal is an offence under the Business Registration Ordinance; a person may be liable on summary conviction to a maximum fine of HK$5,000 and imprisonment for up to 6 months. The Inland Revenue Department may issue penalty assessments, impose late fees, and initiate prosecution. Continuous operation without a valid Business Registration Certificate also exposes the company to additional assessments and enforcement action, though administrative strike-off is triggered by Companies Registry processes rather than business-registration default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Hong Kong Profits Tax Return (Tax Return - Corporations, Form BIR51) with audited financial statements, tax computation and supporting schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), Profits Tax Division, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The IRD issues profits tax returns on a staggered basis according to the company's accounting date. The printed deadline on the notice is generally one month from the issue date; if a qualified tax representative is appointed and an extension request is lodged by the prescribed date, the deadline is typically extended to 3 months from the issue date. No separate annual filing date is fixed across all companies.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit the return within the specified period without reasonable defence is an offence under the Inland Revenue Ordinance; the maximum fine is HK$10,000, and where tax has been undercharged, the court may award a further penalty of up to 3 times the amount of undercharged tax. The IRD may also issue a best-of-assessment or estimated assessment under section 59(3) and proceed to collection against the company. Persistent non-compliance does not by itself trigger company strike-off but can lead to prosecution and severe monetary exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return (Form BIR56A with Form IR56B particulars for directors, employees and paid persons)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), Employer's Return Processing Unit, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The Employer's Return is issued annually, generally in April, and must be completed and delivered to the IRD within one month after the date of issue. A nil return is required if there are no reportable employees, unless the IRD explicitly dispenses with filing.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file an Employer's Return is an offence under section 80 of the Inland Revenue Ordinance, punishable by a maximum fine of HK$10,000 and, where tax is undercharged, a penalty up to 3 times the tax undercharged. The IRD may issue estimated assessments against the employer and pursue interest and collection action. This obligation is separate from profits tax and does not trigger strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Significant Controllers Register (SCR) maintenance and availability for inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies Registry and other law enforcement officers (Hong Kong SAR) on demand; no annual filing is made to the Companies Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ongoing obligation with no annual filing deadline. Every change to a significant controller's particulars, or any transfer of shares or control that changes a significant controller, must be recorded in the SCR within 7 days after the company becomes aware of the change. The register must remain at the company's registered office or another prescribed place in Hong Kong and be available during business hours.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain an SCR or to allow inspection by an authorised officer is an offence; the maximum level 4 fine is HK$25,000, with a continuing daily default fine of HK$700 for each day the offence continues. Knowingly making a false or misleading entry may lead to imprisonment. Administrative strike-off is not triggered directly by SCR failures, but the underlying statutory register non-compliance can form a basis for Companies Registry enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting or written resolution procedure for laying financial statements before members
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Members/shareholders of the company and, where applicable, the board of directors; corporate governance body rather than a government agency
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a private company that is required to hold an AGM, the AGM must be held within 9 months after the end of the financial year. If members validly elect to dispense with the AGM or approve written resolutions in accordance with the Companies Ordinance and the company's articles, the financial statements must still be prepared, approved and signed, and copies must be circulated in accordance with the statutory timelines.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The directors are liable for default in laying financial statements before the members; the maximum fine at level 4 is HK$25,000, and continuing default may attract daily fines. Failure to conduct the corporate governance formalities may prevent the company from validly dispatching tax returns and can be cited during Companies Registry investigations, but it does not by itself trigger administrative strike-off if Annual Return filings are otherwise kept current.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622), every Hong Kong-incorporated private company must appoint an independent certified public accountant as auditor and have audited financial statements unless it qualifies as a small private company or a small private company group and no eligible member objects. A private company qualifies as small if it satisfies at least two of the following three conditions in the relevant financial year: (i) total revenue does not exceed HK$10,000,000 (approximately USD 1.28 million); (ii) total assets do not exceed HK$10,000,000 (approximately USD 1.28 million); and (iii

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Two-tier profits tax: 8.25% on the first HKD 2,000,000 of assessable profits and 16.5% on the remainder. Qualifying research and development expenditure receives an enhanced deduction of 300% on the first HKD 2,000,000 and 200% on the remaining qualifying R&D expenditure. Hong Kong has no statutory tax holidays, no free-zone corporate income tax incentives, and no patent box regime. Territorial source taxation applies, so profits sourced outside Hong Kong benefit from the offshore profits doctrine only if the core income-generating activities are genuinely performed outside Hong Kong.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profits Tax Return - Corporations (Form BIR51), filed electronically through the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) eTAX portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The IRD issues the BIR51 after each accounting period; the return must be lodged within one month from the date of issue, or such extended date usually three months granted to authorized tax representatives. Provisional Profits Tax is payable in two instalments according to the Demand Note issued by the IRD; the standard two instalment pattern is normally 75% and 25% of the provisional tax assessed for the year of assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate taxpayer particulars: legal name, business registration number and Inland Revenue file number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File in the name of the Hong Kong limited company, not the Chinese parent or foreign joint-venture partner. The entity may be 100% non-resident owned but remains a Hong Kong resident taxpayer; do not substitute a China taxpayer identification number for the Hong Kong BR number.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Basis period: accounting period commencement date and expiration date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the financial year adopted by the Hong Kong board. Do not truncate the Hong Kong accounting period to match the PRC calendar year without IRD approval. Any change of accounting date must be reported to the IRD in writing; a non-resident shareholder cannot unilaterally impose a consolidation reporting period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit or loss before taxation per audited financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Start with the profit before income tax charge as recorded under HK financial reporting standards. Include all Stripe and ACH billing revenue arising from the PropTech SaaS platform if the services are controlled, performed, or delivered at least partly in Hong Kong. Deferred tax provisions are not the same as current profits tax and must be reconciled in the supporting schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs: non-deductible expenses and accounting provisions that are not allowed for profits tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back depreciation provisions except where capital allowances are claimed, domestic or private expenses, fines and penalties, non-approved donations, and entertainment expenses without business nexus. Intercompany management fees paid to the Chinese parent are non-deductible unless a transfer pricing charge is arm's length, supported by a written agreement and an actual benefit test.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions: income not chargeable to profits tax, including genuine offshore-source profits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only profits with a true Hong Kong source are taxable. For SaaS and PropTech revenues, recurring cloud license income is frequently sourced to where the service is performed, the user is located, or the contract is managed. A claim that revenues are wholly foreign-sourced merely because the end customers are in mainland China is presumptively red-flagged; provide a full source-of-profits statement, mapping every material function, asset and risk to physical locations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital allowances and balancing charges: plant, machinery, computers, servers and acquired intellectual property.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Book depreciation is not deductible. Claim statutory capital allowances under the Inland Revenue Ordinance on purchased servers, hardware and qualifying software assets. Self-developed software prototypes are generally capital in nature; avoid double representing the same R&D spend as both an R&D deduction claim and an internally generated software capital allowance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjusted assessable profit or adjusted loss after all amendments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the result is a loss, it may be carried forward and set off against future profits; for this structured pipeline the carry-forward limit is recorded as 5 years, although Hong Kong law permits indefinite carry-forward. Do not off-set losses of shell subsidiaries or depend on the Chinese parent to absorb Hong Kong losses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Two-tiered profits tax rate calculation, connected corporation restriction, and foreign tax credit/DTA relief.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply 8.25% to the first HKD 2,000,000 and 16.5% to the excess only if no connected corporation has elected the same two-tier concession. Claim foreign tax credits for taxes paid in mainland China on the same profits, attaching the Chinese tax receipts and a Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate where required by the China-Hong Kong Double Tax Arrangement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration by director, secretary or tax representative, and computation of provisional profits tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The digital declaration on eTAX is a legal statement under the Inland Revenue Ordinance. Directors should personally verify every offshore exclusion and transfer pricing claim before signing. Provisional tax is payable based on the assessed profits for the prior year; failure to notify the IRD of reduced expected profits does not stop the provisional tax charge.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the BIR51 without reasonable excuse is punishable under Inland Revenue Ordinance Cap 112 section 80 with a fine of up to HKD 10,000 and a daily default fine of HKD 300. Where incorrect returns are prepared fraudulently or negligently, a penalty equal to up to three times the tax undercharged may be imposed under section 82A. Fraud and willful tax evasion under section 82(1) carry a fine of HKD 100,000, three times the tax undercharged, and imprisonment for three years. Common law conspiracy to defraud the revenue can result in significantly higher criminal exposure for directors who supervise the filing.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% (Hong Kong imposes no domestic withholding tax on dividends paid by a Hong Kong company)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Because Hong Kong does not impose a dividend withholding tax, no prior IRD approval or withholding procedure is required for the Hong Kong JV to pay a dividend to its shareholders.
